```python
_sensor = dht.DHT22(runtime.shared('pin', _pin, ('dht22',), lambda: machine.Pin(_pin)))

async def emit(properties):
    _sensor.measure()
    msg = {'payload': _sensor.temperature(), 'topic': ''}
    msg['humidity'] = _sensor.humidity()
    return msg
```

The sensor is built once, at setup, not on every `emit()` call —
top-level code and `emit` share the same `properties`.

Temperature goes in `payload`, not humidity, because `payload` is the
field the port's declared type (`number`, here) checks against, and
the field a generic downstream node reads — `debug` prints
`msg['payload']` and nothing else, whatever else is in `msg`. Put
whichever value you want wired and type-checked that way in `payload`.
Anything else is a passenger: `humidity` rides along in the same `msg`,
but only a node written to look for it specifically will ever read it.

### `nonlocal`, not `global`

Your file's top-level code doesn't run at true module scope — each node
instance gets its own wrapper function, so two instances of the same
custom type never share state. To keep a value across calls, use
`nonlocal`:

```python
_count = 0

async def emit(properties):
    nonlocal _count
    _count += 1
    return {'payload': _count, 'topic': ''}
```

`global` raises `NameError` here — there's no module-level name to find.

### Pins and buses

Get a pin or bus with `runtime.shared(kind, key, settings, make)`, not by building it yourself. The first node to
ask builds it with `make()`; every later node gets the same object. If a later node asks with different `settings`,
the flow stops with an error naming both, instead of one node quietly changing the pin under another.

```python
_pin = runtime.shared('pin', 5, ('in', 'up'), lambda: machine.Pin(5, machine.Pin.IN, machine.Pin.PULL_UP))
_i2c = runtime.shared('i2c', 0)  # fetch a bus another node in the flow set up
```

The built-in nodes use these settings: `('in', 'none' | 'up' | 'down')` and `('out', 'none')` for pins, and `()`
for an ADC (`runtime.shared('adc', 26, (), lambda: machine.ADC(machine.Pin(26)))`). Pins, ADC, PWM, I2C and SPI all
work this way: see [Hardware is shared](nodes/index.md#hardware-is-shared).

### Sharing a config (I2C bus, touch panel)

A `configRef` property lets your node pick one of the flow's config nodes. Its value in
`properties` is that config's own properties as a dict (or `None` if none is picked), so a custom
I2C node can join the same bus a built-in `i2c`/`bme280` node uses:

```json
{ "name": "bus", "label": "I2C bus", "kind": "configRef", "configType": "thingstudio/config/i2c-bus", "default": "" }
```

```python
_i2c = runtime.shared('i2c', properties['bus']['bus'])  # the flow's shared bus, by its number
```

The bus/pins come from the config; keep the same `runtime.shared` key a built-in would use so a
clash is reported, not silently shared. (Network configs — WiFi, MQTT — expose only the
credential's name, not the secret, so a custom node can't make a WiFi connection from one.)

### Cleanup

If your node opens something that needs closing on redeploy — a socket,
typically — register it:

```python
import socket

_sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
runtime.register_cleanup('my_node_socket', lambda: _sock.close())

async def run(msg, properties):
    _sock.sendto(str(msg['payload']).encode(), ('192.168.1.50', 9000))
```

`runtime` is already available — no import needed. Without cleanup, a
redeployed flow can leave the old socket open and fail with
`EADDRINUSE` on the next deploy.

### Persisting values

`runtime.settings` keeps a value across reboots and redeploys of the same flow. Use it for an application
setting a user changes on the device — units, a colour scheme — not for per-message state, which belongs in a
closure local.

```python
async def run(msg, properties):
    units = runtime.settings.get('units', 'kg')   # the default is yours, not the store's
    runtime.settings.set('units', msg['payload'])
    msg['payload'] = units
    return msg
```

Values are namespaced by the deployed flow's name, so a different flow cannot read or overwrite them. Renaming
the flow starts a fresh namespace. A missing key returns your default. `set` raises `SettingsError` if the board
cannot save (full or read-only flash) — let it surface as a node error rather than assuming the write worked.
`delete(key)` and `keys()` round out the surface.

The store is a plain key/value; it does not know what a value means. Save only what the user changed, and supply
the default at the read. To clear stored values, see [debugging](debugging.md#commands-and-the-python-prompt).

### Event-driven sources

A `source` that reacts to something other than the clock sets `"eventSource": true` and defines a
second function, `async def wait(properties)`, alongside `emit`. `wait` is awaited, so it blocks
until your event fires; then `emit` builds the message. No `intervalMs` is needed.

```json
{
  "type": "custom/button",
  "kind": "source",
  "label": "button",
  "eventSource": true,
  "ports": { "outputs": [{ "name": "msg", "type": "bool" }] },
  "properties": [{ "name": "pin", "label": "pin", "kind": "pin", "default": 11, "pinUse": "input" }]
}
```

A hardware interrupt (`machine.Pin.irq`) is the usual reason to use `eventSource`. Bridge it into `asyncio`
with the vendored `ThreadSafeEvent` — its `set()` is the one call safe in a hard-IRQ handler — and
register the handler:

```python
import machine
from threadsafe_event import ThreadSafeEvent   # pushed with the flow because you import it

_evt = ThreadSafeEvent()

def _irq(_pin):
    _evt.set()          # a hard-IRQ handler may only do this: no allocation, no print, nothing else

_pin = runtime.shared('pin', properties['pin'], ('in', 'up'),
                      lambda: machine.Pin(properties['pin'], machine.Pin.IN, machine.Pin.PULL_UP))
_pin.irq(trigger=machine.Pin.IRQ_RISING, handler=_irq)

async def wait(properties):
    await _evt.wait()
    _evt.clear()

async def emit(properties):
    return {'payload': True, 'topic': ''}
```

`runtime.asyncio.Event()` is fine when the event is set from other asyncio code; for a real IRQ use
`ThreadSafeEvent`, which survives the hard-IRQ context.

Keep any state the two share at the top of the file (both functions come from one per-instance
closure, so `nonlocal` works across them).

### Run-once sources

A source that runs once, at flow start, sets `"runOnce": true` instead. It defines only `emit`; Thingstudio calls
it once, with no `intervalMs` and no `wait`.

```json
{
  "type": "custom/boot",
  "kind": "source",
  "label": "boot",
  "runOnce": true,
  "ports": { "outputs": [{ "name": "msg", "type": "string" }] }
}
```

### Two-faced nodes

A `sink` with `"eventSource": true` both consumes and produces: one input, one output, and three functions in
`.node.py`. `run(msg, properties)` handles the input; `wait(properties)` then `emit(properties)` produce the
output. All three come from the same per-instance closure, so they share state through `nonlocal`.

```json
{
  "type": "custom/gateway",
  "kind": "sink",
  "label": "gateway",
  "eventSource": true,
  "ports": {
    "inputs": [{ "name": "msg", "type": "any" }],
    "outputs": [{ "name": "msg", "type": "string" }]
  }
}
```

Use it when the node has to react to messages and also act on its own (a clock that echoes a message and then
ticks, or a subscription you can change at run time). A `transform` cannot be two-faced.

## Compile time: `<name>.compile.py`

A package can also include an optional compile-time hook, `<name>.compile.py`, defining one function:

```python
def compile(ctx, properties):
    return {"properties": {...}, "errors": [...]}
```

It runs in the editor when the flow is compiled — never on the board. `properties` is what the flow file holds
for this node; `ctx` describes the flow:

- `ctx["node"]` — this instance: `id`, `type`, `properties`, and `wired` (a boolean per input/output).
- `ctx["flow"]["nodes"]` / `["configs"]` — every node and config, with non-secret properties only.
- `ctx["nodesOfType"]` — every node of this node's type in the flow, including this one: `id`, `type`, and
  non-secret `properties`. Use it when the nodes share a decision (for example, a port's set of routes).
- `ctx["referencedConfigs"]` — the full properties (including credentials) of the configs this node's `configRef`
  fields point at.
- `ctx["target"]` — the board/processor being compiled for, or `None`.

Return a dict (or `None`). Everything is optional:

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `properties` | Extra values merged into what `.node.py` receives. Keys your descriptor doesn't declare are allowed. |
| `claims` | `[{"resource": "GPIO 22", "use": "my device"}]`, checked like a `pin` field. |
| `warnings` | Strings shown in the compile warnings. |
| `errors` | Strings that stop the compile, naming the node. |

The hook is sandboxed: no files, network, clock or randomness. Its result is data only — it cannot return Python
or change the generated code's shape. Limits: 64 KB of properties, 64 claims, 32 warnings and 32 errors, and one
second per hook; a hook that runs too long is stopped.

`wifi status` is an example: its hook derives the flow's WiFi config and whether an MQTT node is present, so its
Python never asks you for the network twice.

## Errors

**Load time** — a malformed `.node.json` is rejected immediately, with
a message naming what's wrong: bad `type`, wrong port count, missing
`intervalMs`, and so on.

**Compile time** — a bad property value on a specific node instance
(e.g. a non-numeric `number` field) errors out naming that node and
property.

**Deploy time** — `.node.py` is spliced into the flow as-is;
Thingstudio doesn't check it. A typo surfaces as a runtime error (e.g.
`NameError`) reported from the device, attributed to your node.

## Limitations

A polled `source` node's `emit` runs on a fixed `intervalMs` schedule; an `eventSource` source waits on `wait` instead.

Two instances of the same custom node get independent setup. For a `pin` field that declares `pinUse`,
Thingstudio checks it against the board and claims it at compile time; a pin you build in Python yourself (or
read from a plain `number` field) it can't see, so use `runtime.shared()` for those, and a clash is caught when
the flow starts.

Custom node Python runs with the same trust as any other node, including Thingstudio's `function` node. Loading a
package only adds it to the palette; its Python runs on a board only when you place the node and deploy. Only files
you place in the folder are loaded — there's no registry and no URL install — so don't put a package there that you
haven't read.


---

Source: https://docs.thingstudio.net/ai-authoring/

# Writing flows with an AI assistant

This page is for an AI assistant (or a person) writing a Thingstudio flow file or a custom node in the user's folder,
without the editor. It is complete on its own, with two companions: the generated [node catalog](nodes-catalog.md), and
the `thingstudio-compile` command ([Check a flow without the editor](check-a-flow.md)). With a board attached,
`device_cli.py` deploys and runs the flow ([Command line](command-line.md#deploy-and-run-a-flow-without-the-editor)).
The whole docs set is also one file at `/llms-full.txt` on the docs site, with an index at `/llms.txt`.

## Setting up your assistant

Paste this into the assistant's standing instructions (a project's instructions, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, or a custom
GPT/Gem), so it reads this page before it writes a flow:

```text
When I ask for a Thingstudio flow or custom node, first read the Thingstudio authoring guide:
https://docs.thingstudio.net/ai-authoring/ (the whole docs set is one file at https://docs.thingstudio.net/llms-full.txt).
Write the flow as a .flow.json file, run the thingstudio-compile check with --board for my board,
fix every error until it prints OK, then tell me: the board id you checked against, which credential
names I must create, what you assumed about wiring, and what you could not check.
Never say a flow works on the board unless you deployed it there and saw its output; otherwise say it
passes the check. No HTTPS in http_request.
```

Claude users can instead save the same text as a skill. The check needs Node and the built `thingstudio-compile.mjs`.

## The loop

1. Write the flow as a `.flow.json` file.
2. Run `node dist-cli/thingstudio-compile.mjs --board board:lolin-s2-mini my.flow.json` (the board ids are `board:cyd`, `board:freenove-s3-4in`,
   `board:lolin-s2-mini`, `board:pico`, `board:pico-2` and `board:pico-w`, or `processor:esp32`, `esp32-c3`, `esp32-s2`,
   `esp32-s3`, `rp2040`, `rp2350` for a bare chip; `--list-boards` shows the current list). Read every error: it names the node and
   says what is wrong. Fix them all and run it again until it prints `OK`.
3. Tell the user to open the file in the editor (**File → Open**), choose the board, and deploy. If a board is
   attached and the user asks you to test it, deploy it with
   [`device_cli.py`](command-line.md#deploy-and-run-a-flow-without-the-editor) instead, and report what the board
   printed. That result is for that board only.

The check is the same compile the editor runs, so a flow that passes it opens and compiles in the editor. It can't
check credentials, custom node packages or the hardware. Don't claim a flow works on a board unless you deployed it
there and saw it run; otherwise say it passes the check.

## The flow file

A JSON object. These keys matter:

| Key | What |
| --- | --- |
| `formatVersion` | `1` |
| `flowName` | A name for the flow. |
| `nodes` | `[{ "id", "type", "properties" }]`. `id` is any unique string. `type` is `thingstudio/<kind>`. |
| `edges` | `[[fromId, outputNumber, toId, inputNumber]]`. Numbers start at 0, in the order the [catalog](nodes-catalog.md) lists the ports. |
| `configs` | `[{ "id", "type", "properties" }]`: shared settings (I2C bus, WiFi, MQTT broker, touch panel). |
| `screens` | The pages of any GUI screen, keyed by that node's id. See [GUI](#gui-screens). |
| `panes`, `paneOf` | Optional. Tabs in the editor and which tab each node is on; leave them out and everything lands on one tab. When you edit a file that has them, put new nodes in `paneOf` too (copy the pattern). |
| `layout` | `{ "<nodeId>": { "pos": [x, y] } }`. Optional, but give positions: without them every node lands at 0,0. |
| `notes` | Optional text shown in the editor's Notes panel. Say what the flow is for and how it is wired. |

A property you leave out gets the default listed in the [catalog](nodes-catalog.md). Use the catalog's names and types
exactly: `intervalMs`, not `interval`. Values and ranges are checked by the compile, which says what is allowed.

Place the nodes left to right, sources on the left and sinks on the right, about 220 px apart, so the user can read
the flow when they open it.

A complete flow, a blinking LED on a LOLIN S2 Mini (its LED is pin 15):

```json
{
  "formatVersion": 1,
  "flowName": "blink",
  "nodes": [
    { "id": "tick", "type": "thingstudio/timer", "properties": { "intervalMs": 500 } },
    { "id": "flip", "type": "thingstudio/function",
      "properties": { "code": "msg['payload'] = msg['payload'] % 2\nreturn msg", "outputCount": 1 } },
    { "id": "led", "type": "thingstudio/gpio_out", "properties": { "pin": 15 } }
  ],
  "edges": [["tick", 0, "flip", 0], ["flip", 0, "led", 0]],
  "layout": { "tick": { "pos": [80, 200] }, "flip": { "pos": [300, 200] }, "led": { "pos": [520, 200] } },
  "configs": []
}
```

## Which node

| To... | Use |
| --- | --- |
| send a message every so often, or once at start | `timer`, `startup`, `inject` |
| read a BME280 / BMP280 | `bme280` (payload is a dict with `temperature`, `humidity`, `pressure`; pick one out in a `function`) |
| read another I2C chip | `i2c` on a shared `i2c-bus` config |
| react to a switch or button | `eswitch` (a debounced switch: open and close events); `ebutton` for press, release, long-press and double-click; `interrupt` for raw edges |
| drive a pin | `gpio_out` (on/off), `pwm_out` |
| change or route a message | `function`; `filter` to pass only changes; `delay` |
| keep a number's history | `journal`, shown by a `gui_trend` |
| show the time | `ntp` (two for time and date: `format` `time` and `date`) |
| talk MQTT / HTTP / UDP | `mqtt_publish`, `mqtt_subscribe`, `http_request`, `http_in` and `http_response`, `udp_send`, `udp_receive` |
| draw on a screen | `gui_screen` with `gui_*` widgets, wired to `display_spi` |

## Messages and the function node

Every message is a dict: `msg = {'payload': ..., 'topic': ...}`. `payload` is what nodes read; `topic` is a string, `''`
when there is nothing to say. Other keys ride along.

A function node's `code` is the body of a function in MicroPython (a subset of Python with a small standard library). Return `msg` to pass it on, or `None` to stop. With `outputCount` above 1, return a list with one
entry per output (`None` for nothing, a list of messages for several). `context` keeps state for the node, `flow` for
the whole flow. See [function](nodes/function.md). A syntax error in the code is caught by the check.

A wire is refused if the payload types can't meet (for example a `bool` into a `bytes` input). The check reports it.
Numbers go into `bool` inputs (zero is off), and an `int` into a `number`; a `number` into an `int` is refused.

Addresses are written two ways, because the nodes differ: the `bme280` `address` is a plain number (`118` is `0x76`);
a touch panel config's `address` is text (`"0x38"`). The [catalog](nodes-catalog.md) notes which.

A node that uses the network (`mqtt_publish`, `http_request`, `http_in` and so on) uses the flow's WiFi: add a WiFi config to
`configs` and it is picked up; the node has no WiFi property of its own.

Things to know before you pick a node:

- `http_request` is plain `http://` only (no HTTPS), GET or POST. A reply with any status is passed on with an integer
  `msg['status']`; a failed connection or a timeout sends nothing on and logs an error. So test `msg['status'] == 200`
  in a `function`, and expect no message at all when the server is unreachable.
- `mqtt_subscribe` payloads arrive as text when they decode, otherwise bytes. For a number, use `float(msg['payload'])`
  in a `function`.
- `function` code can `import` standard modules (`json`, `framebuf`, `time`) inside the body.
- `http_in` gives a `payload` of `None` and `http_response` sets no `Content-Type`. Use port 80 unless something else
  on the board already uses it.
- `bme280` has no input: it reads on its own interval. To answer a web request with a current value, keep the
  latest reading with `flow.set('temp', ...)` in a `function` after the sensor, and read it with `flow.get('temp')`
  in a `function` between `http_in` and `http_response` (send a 503 before the first reading arrives).
- To print text on a `display_i2c` (SSD1306), draw with `framebuf` in a `function` and send the buffer: see
  [display i2c](nodes/display-i2c.md#text-on-the-panel). Its address property is `addr`, a plain number (`60` is `0x3C`).

## Pins: take them from the board

Never guess a pin. List the boards with `--list-boards`, run `--board-info board:<id>` for what each pin does (the
LED, the buttons, the display, the I2C pins) and which to avoid, and check the finished flow with `--board board:<id>`. If the user's board is not listed, say so, ask for the pins, and point them to the MicroPython documentation
for their board (docs.micropython.org). Don't pretend a board is supported.

Things the pin check cannot catch: a pin that exists but is wired to something else on the user's board. When the
user has told you the wiring, use it; when they haven't, say what you assumed.

## Config nodes and credentials

A node that needs shared settings names a config by id: `"i2cConfigId": "cfg-i2c"`, with the config in `configs`:

```json
{ "id": "cfg-i2c", "type": "thingstudio/config/i2c-bus", "properties": { "bus": 0, "scl": 15, "sda": 16, "freq": 100000 } }
```

The [catalog](nodes-catalog.md) lists each config type's fields. WiFi and MQTT configs hold a **credential name**:

```json
{ "id": "cfg-wifi", "type": "thingstudio/config/wifi", "properties": { "credentialName": "home", "security": "password" } }
```

**Never write a password, SSID or broker secret into a flow file.** Write a `credentialName` and tell the user which
names to create in the editor's credential store (they are saved there, not in the file). The check uses stand-ins
for them and says so.

## GUI screens

A touch or plain display is two nodes wired together, `gui_screen` then `display_spi`, plus widget nodes (`gui_label`,
`gui_readout`, `gui_bar`, `gui_trend`, `gui_led`, `gui_button`) that you wire data into. Where each widget sits is in
`screens`:

```json
"screens": { "<screenId>": { "pages": [
  { "name": "main", "root": { "kind": "column", "gap": 6, "padding": 4, "children": [
    { "kind": "text", "text": "Living room", "font": "font_body20" },
    { "kind": "widget", "node": "<readoutId>", "font": "font_digits48", "unitsFont": "font_body24", "alignSelf": "center" },
    { "kind": "spacer", "grow": 1 },
    { "kind": "pagedots", "alignSelf": "center" }
  ] } }
] } }
```

Rules that cause most failures:

- The screen's `width` and `height` are the **panel's own size** (320 × 480 for the Freenove 4") whatever the orientation.
  Portrait needs nothing more: leave `orientation` empty and use the board's `rotation` (1 for the Freenove). To turn
  the picture, set the `orientation` property of `display_spi` to `"90"`, `"180"` or `"270"` (clockwise), not the
  screen's size.
- A navigate button's `target` is `next`, `prev`, `back`, `home` or the `name` of a page in `screens`; when you edit an
  existing flow, read the page names from its `screens` section.
- Fonts: `font_body12/16/20/24`, `font_digits16/24/32/48/64` (digits and a few symbols only), `font_seg748/64/96`
  (seven-segment: `0-9 : . -` and space). A character a font doesn't have is an error.
- A widget is placed once per page, drawn the same on every page it is on. A label shows a value up to `maxChars` wide.
- A page that doesn't fit gives an error that names the widget and page and how many pixels it needs. Use a smaller
  font or fewer things per row. Rows need the screen width minus the container's padding (in landscape on a
  320-wide panel that is under 312 px).
- With an `orientation`, `xstart` and `ystart` must be `-1`, which means "no offset" (the CYD example flow uses 0,
  which an orientation refuses; `-1` is always allowed). At `"90"` or `"270"` the picture is the panel turned, so a
  320 x 480 panel gives 480 wide by 320 high to lay out.
- A modal is laid out in `screens.<screenId>.modals`, not in `pages`: see the format below.
- A trend takes a journal's first output, and a journal takes numbers: `sensor → journal → trend`.

A modal (`gui_modal`, with `screen` set to the `gui_screen` node's id) is listed next to `pages`. Its `root` holds what
it shows, and not the modal node itself:

```json
"modals": [ { "node": "<modalNodeId>", "root": { "kind": "column", "padding": 8, "children": [
  { "kind": "text", "text": "Too hot", "font": "font_body24" },
  { "kind": "widget", "node": "<labelId>", "font": "font_body20", "maxChars": 20 }
] } } ]
```

Any message opens it; a message with `payload` `None` closes it; `timeout` (seconds, `0` for never) closes it by
itself; a navigate button with `target` `back` acknowledges it. Its output sends `'ack'`, `'timeout'` or `'closed'`.

Placement keys, in `screens`:

| Element | Keys |
| --- | --- |
| `row`, `column` | `children`, `gap`, `padding`, `align`, `justify`, `grow`, `alignSelf` |
| `widget` | `node` (the widget node's id), `font`, `unitsFont` (readout), `align` and `maxChars` (label), `height` and `minWidth` (bar, trend), `diameter` (light), `grow`, `alignSelf` |
| `text` | `text`, `font`, `align` |
| `pagedots`, `spacer` | `diameter`, `gap`; `width`, `height`, `grow` |

A button widget takes `font`, `grow` and `alignSelf` like the others. The button's own behaviour (`mode`, `target`,
`onValue`, ...) is on the node: see the [catalog](nodes-catalog.md). For a toggle that follows a real device (a smart
plug), `gui.md` has the wiring.

Read [GUI nodes](nodes/gui.md) for the details, and copy from `test-flows/`:
`gui-headliner-sensor-freenove-s3-4in.flow.json` (a sensor display with trends, a clock and MQTT),
`gui-touch-freenove-s3-4in.flow.json` (buttons), `gui-orientation-test-freenove-s3-4in.flow.json`.

## Custom nodes

If no node does the job and a function node is not enough, write a custom node: `<name>.node.json` and
`<name>.node.py`. [Writing custom nodes](custom-nodes.md) is complete on its own. The two files go in `~/.thingstudio/custom-nodes/` on the
computer running Thingstudio. The check command can't check them: read them against that page, and test the
Python body on its own with sample messages.

## Examples to copy

| Task | File in `test-flows/` |
| --- | --- |
| Blink an LED | `blink.flow.json` |
| Publish to MQTT | `basic-mqtt.flow.json` |
| Call a web service | `basic-http-request.flow.json` |
| A BME280 reading | `bmp280-test-flow.flow.json` |
| A sensor on a display, with trends and a clock | `gui-headliner-sensor-freenove-s3-4in.flow.json` |
| Touch buttons | `gui-touch-freenove-s3-4in.flow.json` |

## When you hand the flow back

Tell the user, briefly: that it passes the check (and with which `--board`), which credential names to create, which
board to choose in the editor, what you assumed about wiring, and what you could not check.


---

Source: https://docs.thingstudio.net/check-a-flow/

# Check a flow without the editor

`thingstudio-compile` compiles and checks a flow file from the command line, with the same errors the editor gives.
Use it in a script, in CI, or to let an AI assistant check a flow it has written.

## Build it

From the `editor/` folder:

```text
npm ci
npm run build:cli
```

This writes `dist-cli/thingstudio-compile.mjs`, one script that needs only Node 22 or later.

## Use it

```text
node dist-cli/thingstudio-compile.mjs my-flow.flow.json
```

A good flow prints one line:

```text
OK  my-flow.flow.json: 25 nodes, 21 wires, 4 configs, 38980 bytes of MicroPython, 0 warnings
```

A bad one lists every problem it found:

```text
FAIL  my-flow.flow.json: 2 errors
  error: wire from node t1 output 4 to node g1 input 1: node t1 has no output 4 (it has 1)
  error: node x1: unknown node type "thingstudio/teleporter"
```

The exit code is 0 for a valid flow, 1 for a flow with errors, and 2 for a bad command or a file it can't read.

## Options

- `--board board:freenove-s3-4in` checks pins against that board. `--list-boards` shows the choices. Without a
  board, pins are checked against the widest range and a warning says so.
- `--board-info board:freenove-s3-4in` prints that board's labelled pins (the LED, the display, the I2C pins), the
  GPIOs that exist, and the ones to avoid or that are reserved, as JSON.
- `--out flow.py` writes the generated MicroPython.
- `--json` prints the result as JSON: `ok`, `errors`, `warnings`, `notes`, `stats` and the `source`.
- `--strict` makes warnings fail the check.
- `--describe timer` prints a node's type, ports and properties with their defaults. `--describe-all` prints every
  node and config node (add `--json` for JSON). The same list is on the [node catalog](nodes-catalog.md) page,
  generated from the code.
- `--no-syntax` skips the MicroPython syntax check. `--arch` sets its `-march` (default `xtensawin`).

## What it checks

- The file is a flow file, and every node type exists.
- Every wire joins real ports, and is one the editor would accept. The editor drops a wire it refuses when it opens the file.
- A property the file leaves out gets the editor's default, as when you open the file in the editor.
- The flow compiles: pins, properties, GUI layouts, nodes with nothing wired to them.
- The generated code is valid MicroPython. This uses the same `mpy-cross` the editor deploys with, and catches a
  typo in a function node's code before you deploy.

## What it doesn't check

- **WiFi and MQTT credentials.** The secrets are in the backend, so the check uses stand-in values and says so in a
  note. A missing credential shows up when you open the flow in the editor.
- **Custom node packages.** A flow that uses one fails with "unknown node type".
- **A real board.** It can't tell you the display is wired right, or that the memory is enough. Deploy does that;
  [Command line](command-line.md#deploy-and-run-a-flow-without-the-editor) can deploy and run a flow without the
  editor.


---

Source: https://docs.thingstudio.net/command-line/

# Command line

Options for starting Thingstudio, a way to install the runtime and run flows without the editor, and a check for a
flow file. To check a flow file from the command line, see [Check a flow without the editor](check-a-flow.md).

## Starting options

Add these after `thingstudio` (or `thingstudio-backend`, from source). `thingstudio --help` lists them all.

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--no-browser` | Don't open the editor in a browser. Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` yourself. |
| `--port N` | Serve the editor on port `N` instead of 8765. |
| `--data-dir DIR` | Use `DIR` instead of `~/.thingstudio`. See [The Thingstudio folder](thingstudio-folder.md#using-a-different-folder). |
| `--log-level LEVEL` | How much Thingstudio prints in its terminal: `DEBUG`, `INFO` (default), `WARNING` or `ERROR`. |

If you restart Thingstudio with the editor still open, that tab reconnects and no new one opens.

## Installing the runtime from the command line

Useful for scripting, or setting up several boards at once. It needs a copy of the source repository. Click
**Disconnect** in the editor first, so the port is free.

```sh
pip install mpremote
python3 test-flows/deploy_runtime.py --port PORT
```

`PORT` is the board's port, as shown in the editor's port list. When it finishes, click **Connect** in the editor.

`device_cli.py runtime install` does the same thing and resets the board afterwards; see below.

## Deploy and run a flow without the editor

`device_cli.py` is a small command line for a board on USB serial. It does what the editor does, without a browser:
find the board, check the runtime, deploy a flow, fire inject nodes, run console commands and watch the output.

```sh
python3 test-flows/device_cli.py list          # USB serial ports
python3 test-flows/device_cli.py hello         # runtime version, chip, running flow
python3 test-flows/device_cli.py flow deploy my-flow.flow.json \
    --mpy-cross ~/mpy-src/mpy-cross/build/mpy-cross
python3 test-flows/device_cli.py trigger inject0001
python3 test-flows/device_cli.py exec "settings.namespaces()"
python3 test-flows/device_cli.py watch
```

- If there is one USB serial port, `--port` is not needed. Use `--port` or `THINGSTUDIO_PORT` otherwise.
- `flow deploy` compiles the `.flow.json` with the same compiler as the editor, then deploys it. It takes the flow
  name from the file's own `flowName`. That name is also the `settings` namespace, so check it is what you expect.
- `--trigger NODE_ID` (repeatable) fires inject or startup nodes after deploy, for testing without clicking.
- `--json` prints one JSON object per line, for scripts.
- Disconnect in the editor first: only one program can hold the serial port.
- `flow deploy` needs a native `mpy-cross`. The build recipe is in `device-runtime/test/README.md`, or set
  `THINGSTUDIO_MPY_CROSS` to one you already have.

`python3 test-flows/device_cli.py <command> --help` lists every option. `test-flows/README.md` has ready-made test
flows and their expected output.


---

Source: https://docs.thingstudio.net/nodes-catalog/

# Node catalog

<!-- Generated by `node dist-cli/thingstudio-compile.mjs --describe-all --markdown`. Do not edit by hand: a test fails when it is out of date. -->

Every node a flow file can use: its type id, its ports with their payload types, and its properties with the default
the editor gives a new node. A property a flow file leaves out gets this default. Allowed values and ranges are
checked when the flow is compiled, and the error says what is allowed. See [Check a flow without the editor](check-a-flow.md).

Ports are numbered from 0 in a flow file's `edges`: `[fromNodeId, outputNumber, toNodeId, inputNumber]`, in the order listed here.

## general

### change

Type `thingstudio/change`, kind transform, palette group general.

- Inputs: msg (any)
- Outputs: msg (any)
- Properties (name, type, default):
    - `operation`, string, default `"set"`
    - `scope`, string, default `"msg"`
    - `property`, string, default `"payload"`
    - `valueFrom`, string, default `"literal"`
    - `valueType`, string, default `"string"`
    - `value`, string, default `""`

### debug

Type `thingstudio/debug`, kind sink, palette group general.

- Inputs: msg (any)
- Outputs: none
- Properties (name, type, default):
    - `fullMessage`, boolean, default `false`

### delay

Type `thingstudio/delay`, kind transform, palette group general.

- Inputs: msg (any)
- Outputs: msg (any)
- Properties (name, type, default):
    - `delayMs`, number, default `1000`

### filter

Type `thingstudio/filter`, kind transform, palette group general.

- Inputs: msg (any)
- Outputs: msg (any)
- Properties (name, type, default):
    - `mode`, string, default `"change"`
    - `threshold`, number, default `1`
    - `intervalMs`, number, default `1000`
    - `ignoreFirst`, boolean, default `false`
    - `perTopic`, boolean, default `true`

### function

Type `thingstudio/function`, kind transform, palette group general.

- Inputs: msg (any)
- Outputs: msg (any) (the number of outputs is the node's `outputCount` property)
- Properties (name, type, default):
    - `code`, string, default `"msg['payload'] = msg['payload']\nreturn msg\n"` — the body of a MicroPython function; `msg` in, return the message, None, or a list with one entry per output
    - `outputCount`, number, default `1` — how many outputs, 1 to 10

### inject

Type `thingstudio/inject`, kind source, palette group general.

- Inputs: none
- Outputs: msg (bool)
- Properties (name, type, default):
    - `payloadType`, string, default `"bool"`
    - `payloadValue`, string, default `"true"`

### journal

Type `thingstudio/journal`, kind transform, palette group general.

- Inputs: msg (any)
- Outputs: series (any), rollup (any)
- Properties (name, type, default):
    - `rows`, number, default `60` — how many rows are kept, 1 to 256
    - `stepSeconds`, number, default `60` — seconds per row; 0 makes every message its own row
    - `steps`, number, default `0` — rows per roll-up to the second output; 0 sends none
    - `xff`, number, default `0.5` — 0 to 1: a roll-up becomes a gap if more than this fraction of its rows are gaps

### startup

Type `thingstudio/startup`, kind source, palette group general.

- Inputs: none
- Outputs: msg (bool)
- Properties (name, type, default):
    - `payloadType`, string, default `"bool"`
    - `payloadValue`, string, default `"true"`

### timer

Type `thingstudio/timer`, kind source, palette group general.

- Inputs: none
- Outputs: msg (int)
- Properties (name, type, default):
    - `intervalMs`, number, default `1000` — milliseconds between messages; the payload is a count that rises 1, 2, 3...

## GUI

### bar

Type `thingstudio/gui_bar`, kind sink, palette group GUI.

- Inputs: msg (any)
- Outputs: none
- Properties (name, type, default):
    - `name`, string, default `""`
    - `lo`, number, default `0` — the value at which the bar is empty
    - `hi`, number, default `100` — the value at which the bar is full
    - `staleAfter`, number, default `0` — seconds without a new value before it dims; 0 = never

### button

Type `thingstudio/gui_button`, kind sink, palette group GUI.

- Inputs: msg (any)
- Outputs: msg (any)
- Properties (name, type, default):
    - `name`, string, default `""`
    - `mode`, string, default `"momentary"` — momentary, toggle or navigate
    - `valueType`, string, default `"bool"` — bool, string or number: the type of what it sends
    - `fireOn`, string, default `"release"` — release (default: the finger lifts inside the button) or press
    - `text`, string, default `""` — what is drawn on the button; empty uses `name`
    - `value`, string, default `""` — momentary: what it sends; empty sends true, 'ON' or 1 by valueType
    - `maxChars`, number, default `8` — room for this many characters (a value replaces the text)
    - `onValue`, string, default `""` — toggle: what it sends to turn on
    - `offValue`, string, default `""` — toggle: what it sends to turn off
    - `onText`, string, default `"ON"`
    - `offText`, string, default `"OFF"`
    - `initial`, boolean, default `false`
    - `pendingTimeout`, number, default `5` — toggle with a wired input: seconds to wait for the input to confirm before going back
    - `target`, string, default `""` — navigate: next, prev, back, home or a page name from `screens`

### label

Type `thingstudio/gui_label`, kind sink, palette group GUI.

- Inputs: msg (any)
- Outputs: none
- Properties (name, type, default):
    - `name`, string, default `""`
    - `maxChars`, number, default `8` — room for this many characters
    - `staleAfter`, number, default `0` — seconds without a new value before it dims; 0 = never

### light

Type `thingstudio/gui_led`, kind sink, palette group GUI.

- Inputs: msg (any)
- Outputs: none
- Properties (name, type, default):
    - `name`, string, default `""`
    - `staleAfter`, number, default `0` — seconds without a new value before it goes grey; 0 = never

### modal

Type `thingstudio/gui_modal`, kind sink, palette group GUI.

- Inputs: msg (any)
- Outputs: msg (any)
- Properties (name, type, default):
    - `name`, string, default `""`
    - `screen`, string, default `""` — the id of the gui_screen node this modal belongs to
    - `priority`, number, default `0` — a higher priority takes the screen from a lower one; the other waits
    - `timeout`, number, default `0` — seconds before the modal closes itself; 0 never

### navigator

Type `thingstudio/gui_navigator`, kind transform, palette group GUI.

- Inputs: msg (any)
- Outputs: page (string)
- Properties (name, type, default):
    - `name`, string, default `"navigator"`
    - `screen`, string, default `""`

### readout

Type `thingstudio/gui_readout`, kind sink, palette group GUI.

- Inputs: msg (any)
- Outputs: none
- Properties (name, type, default):
    - `name`, string, default `""`
    - `units`, string, default `""` — text shown after the number
    - `decimals`, number, default `1`
    - `lo`, number, default `0` — lowest value it will show; with hi, sizes the space the number gets
    - `hi`, number, default `100` — highest value it will show; with lo, sizes the space the number gets
    - `staleAfter`, number, default `0` — seconds without a new value before it dims; 0 = never

### screen

Type `thingstudio/gui_screen`, kind source, palette group GUI.

- Inputs: none
- Outputs: frame (bytes)
- Properties (name, type, default):
    - `name`, string, default `"screen"`
    - `minInterval`, number, default `200` — least milliseconds between screen updates
    - `wrap`, boolean, default `true` — whether next/prev wrap around at the ends of the pages
    - `touchPanelConfigId`, string, default `""`, the id of a `thingstudio/config/touch-panel` config — the touch-panel config to read touches from; empty for none

### trend

Type `thingstudio/gui_trend`, kind sink, palette group GUI.

- Inputs: msg (any)
- Outputs: none
- Properties (name, type, default):
    - `name`, string, default `""`
    - `lo`, number, default `0` — value at the bottom of the bars; the range is fixed
    - `hi`, number, default `100` — value at the top of the bars; the range is fixed
    - `columns`, number, default `60` — natural width in bars; in a layout it can stretch to show more
    - `colWidth`, number, default `3` — pixels per bar
    - `height`, number, default `48` — natural height in pixels
    - `staleAfter`, number, default `0` — seconds without a new row before it dims; 0 = never

## hardware

### adc

Type `thingstudio/adc`, kind source, palette group hardware.

- Inputs: none
- Outputs: msg (any)
- Properties (name, type, default):
    - `pin`, number, default `34` — the ADC pin to read; on ESP32, use an ADC1 pin if the flow uses WiFi (ADC2 can't with the radio on)
    - `mode`, string, default `"relative"` — relative (current value +- delta) or absolute (lower..upper)
    - `delta`, number, default `2000` — relative mode: how far the reading must move from the last sent one to fire
    - `lower`, number, default `0` — absolute mode: the low bound
    - `upper`, number, default `50000` — absolute mode: the high bound
    - `sense`, string, default `"outside"` — outside (fire when the value leaves the bounds) or inside (fire when it returns)
    - `pollMs`, number, default `0` — also send every this many ms; 0 = only on a bounds crossing

### bme280

Type `thingstudio/bme280`, kind source, palette group hardware.

- Inputs: none
- Outputs: msg (any)
- Properties (name, type, default):
    - `i2cConfigId`, string, default `""`, the id of a `thingstudio/config/i2c-bus` config
    - `address`, number, default `118` — the I2C address as a plain number: 118 is 0x76, 119 is 0x77
    - `intervalMs`, number, default `5000` — milliseconds between readings, at least 100

### display i2c

Type `thingstudio/display_i2c`, kind sink, palette group hardware.

- Inputs: frame (bytes)
- Outputs: none
- Properties (name, type, default):
    - `controller`, string, default `"ssd1306"`
    - `i2cConfigId`, string, default `""`, the id of a `thingstudio/config/i2c-bus` config
    - `addr`, number, default `60` — the I2C address as a plain number: 60 is 0x3C, the usual SSD1306 address
    - `width`, number, default `128`
    - `height`, number, default `64`

### display spi

Type `thingstudio/display_spi`, kind sink, palette group hardware.

- Inputs: frame (bytes)
- Outputs: none
- Properties (name, type, default):
    - `orientation`, string, default `""` — empty = off (the raw `rotation`), or 0, 90, 180, 270 as a string: the picture turned clockwise. Portrait 320x480 needs none
    - `controller`, string, default `"st7789"`
    - `frameFormat`, string, default `"rgb565"` — rgb565, gs4, gs2 or mono; must match the gui screen
    - `palette`, object, default `[0,65535,63488,2016,31,65504,2047,63519,33808,16904,50712,64800,32768,1024,16,1040]`
    - `spiBus`, number, default `2`
    - `baudrate`, number, default `40000000`
    - `sck`, number, default `12`
    - `mosi`, number, default `11`
    - `dc`, number, default `13`
    - `cs`, number, default `-1` — GPIO, or -1 for none
    - `reset`, number, default `-1` — GPIO, or -1 for none
    - `backlight`, number, default `-1` — GPIO, or -1 for none
    - `width`, number, default `135` — the panel's own width in pixels
    - `height`, number, default `240` — the panel's own height in pixels
    - `rotation`, number, default `0` — how the panel is mounted, 0 to 7 (MADCTL); with an orientation, 0 to 3 only
    - `colorOrder`, string, default `"bgr"`
    - `invertColors`, boolean, default `false`
    - `dataLatchOrder`, boolean, default `true`
    - `xstart`, number, default `-1` — -1 lets the driver choose; set both only for an unusual panel offset
    - `ystart`, number, default `-1`

### ebutton

Type `thingstudio/ebutton`, kind source, palette group hardware.

- Inputs: none

- Properties (name, type, default):

### encoder

Type `thingstudio/encoder`, kind source, palette group hardware.

- Inputs: none
- Outputs: msg (number)
- Properties (name, type, default):
    - `pinX`, number, default `10` — one of the two quadrature switch pins
    - `pinY`, number, default `11` — the other quadrature switch pin
    - `div`, number, default `1` — divide the count by this to track detents; 1 counts every pulse
    - `value`, number, default `0` — the starting value
    - `vmin`, string, default `""` — lowest value, or blank for no limit
    - `vmax`, string, default `""` — highest value, or blank for no limit
    - `mod`, string, default `""` — wrap the value at this number, or blank for none
    - `delay`, number, default `100` — ms to wait for motion to settle; also limits how often it sends

### ntp

Type `thingstudio/ntp`, kind sink, palette group network.

- Inputs: msg (any)
- Outputs: msg (any)
- Properties (name, type, default):
    - `server`, string, default `"pool.ntp.org"`
    - `utcOffset`, number, default `0` — hours from UTC for standard time, -12 to 14 (5.5 for India); the summer hour is added by `dst`
    - `dst`, string, default `"eu"` — eu adds the UK/EU summer hour automatically; none adds nothing
    - `format`, string, default `"time"` — what goes in payload: unix (int), time (14:05), time_seconds, time_12h (2:05 pm), date (Wed 14 Oct), date_iso, iso. Every message also carries all seven as fields of those names
    - `wifiConfigId`, string, default `""`, the id of a `thingstudio/config/wifi` config

## Config nodes

A config node is listed under `configs` in a flow file as `{id, type, properties}`. A node names it by id in a property such as `i2cConfigId`. Credentials are saved by name (`credentialName`), never as secrets in the file.

### I2C bus

Type `thingstudio/config/i2c-bus`.

- `bus`, number
- `scl`, pin
- `sda`, pin
- `freq`, number: 100000 suits most sensors; 400000 for displays that can take it.

Defaults: `{"bus":0,"scl":null,"sda":null,"freq":100000}`

### MQTT Broker

Type `thingstudio/config/mqtt-broker`.

- `credentialName`, credential

Defaults: `{"credentialName":""}`

### Touch panel

Type `thingstudio/config/touch-panel`.

- `controller`, select: one of `ft6336u`; Other controllers (GT911, CST820) aren't supported yet.
- `i2cConfigId`, configRef: the id of a `thingstudio/config/i2c-bus` config
- `address`, text: 7-bit, e.g. 0x38.
- `rstPin`, pin: Blank if the panel has none.
- `pollMs`, number
- `width`, number
- `height`, number: The panel's own size. If the display is rotated, tick swap/flip until a touch lands where you pressed.
- `swapXY`, boolean
- `flipX`, boolean
- `flipY`, boolean

Defaults: `{"controller":"ft6336u","i2cConfigId":"","address":"0x38","rstPin":"","pollMs":20,"width":320,"height":480,"swapXY":false,"flipX":false,"flipY":false}`

### WiFi

Type `thingstudio/config/wifi`, one per flow.

- `credentialName`, credential
- `security`, select: one of `password`, `open`, `unmanaged`
- `allowReprovisioning`, boolean: Off by default: the device only opens its setup AP on first run. Turning this on lets it reopen that AP any time WiFi drops, not just once -- only do this on a trusted, physically-controlled network. Anyone in radio range while WiFi is down could otherwise connect to the AP and redirect this device to a different network.

Defaults: `{"credentialName":"","security":"password","allowReprovisioning":false}`

Source: https://docs.thingstudio.net/debugging/

# Debugging & troubleshooting

What the console and compiled source show, and what to do when a board or deploy fails.

## Console and compiled source

The **console** shows what the board and Thingstudio report: deploy results, node errors, and what `debug` nodes
and `print()` send. **Clear** empties it.

Its **Show** menu sets how much it shows:

- **Normal:** your flow's output, warnings, errors, and the results of what you do, such as a deploy.
- **Info:** adds routine reports: board detected, versions, memory, libraries sent, network status.
- **Debug:** adds raw protocol messages and the board's boot output.

Hidden lines are kept, so choosing Info or Debug later shows what was already logged.

The **Compiled source** panel shows the MicroPython your flow compiles to.

The editor's version is next to its name in the toolbar, and in **Help → About Thingstudio**. A `+` after it means
you built it from uncommitted changes. Include the versions when you report a problem.

### Memory

With **Show** set to **Info**, a `[memory]` line after each connect and deploy shows the board's free RAM. On an
ESP32 it also shows the ESP-IDF heap and its largest free block. WiFi, MQTT and TLS use the ESP-IDF heap, not
MicroPython's. If WiFi won't join while MicroPython has plenty free, a low ESP-IDF figure is the likely cause. The
[FAQ](faq.md) explains where an ESP32's memory goes.

## Commands and the Python prompt

The command box under the console runs Python on the board. Type a line and press Enter; the result appears in the
console. The up and down arrows bring back earlier commands.

```python
gc.mem_free()
import machine; machine.Pin(15).value()
os.listdir()
```

Commands run alongside your flow, and variables you set stay for the next command. A command that takes time, such
as a `sleep` or a loop, holds up the flow until it finishes.

The stored application values are available as `settings`:

```python
settings.namespaces()      # each flow's name and how many values it holds
settings.clear()           # clear the current flow's values
settings.clear_all()       # clear every flow's values
```

Use these if a saved value is wrong, or a flow you no longer deploy left values behind. Clearing takes effect
immediately; the next read returns the default. **Tools → Clear device settings…** does the same from the editor:
choose the current flow, or every flow.

For MicroPython's own `>>>` prompt, click **Stop flow & open prompt**. The flow and the runtime stop; nothing is
deleted. What you type in the box now goes to that prompt, and Deploy is off. Click **Restart Thingstudio** to start
the runtime and the saved flow again.

To use the prompt from another program, such as Thonny or `mpremote`, click **Connected · Disconnect** first.

### Watching a board start up

To see a board's own startup messages, connect with `mpremote connect PORT` and no further command, or a serial
monitor that doesn't send Ctrl-C when it opens. A working runtime prints `LISTENER_BOOTING`, then
`LISTENER_READY`.

`mpremote repl` and Thonny's Shell interrupt the board as they connect, which looks like a board that never starts.
Close them before connecting from Thingstudio: only one program can use the port at a time.

## Board won't connect

When **Connect**, **Tools → Check status** or **Tools → Install runtime…** gets no proper reply, the console says
what the board sent instead, and what to do:

| Console says | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| Nothing came back | Usually no MicroPython. [Install MicroPython](installing-micropython.md). If it's there, press reset, then **Tools → Check status**. |
| MicroPython but no Thingstudio runtime | **Tools → Install runtime…**. |
| MicroPython replied but didn't enter install mode | Press reset and install again. |
| Board is in its bootloader | An ESP32 in download mode. Press reset, not BOOT. If it repeats, install MicroPython. |
| Board runs CircuitPython, or replied but not as MicroPython | [Install MicroPython](installing-micropython.md). |
| Runtime still starting | Wait, then **Tools → Check status**. |
| Install stalled | Replug the board, click **⟳**, and try again. If it repeats, restart Thingstudio. |

If the port itself won't open, the console says why:

| Console says | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| port in use | Close other serial monitors, IDEs, or editor tabs using the board. |
| port access refused | Replug the board and check port permissions. On Linux, check you're in the `dialout` group. |
| board gone from that port | Check the cable, click **⟳**, and connect again. |

The raw error stays in the message, in brackets. Include it if you report a problem.

## Deploy is grayed out

**Compile → Deploy** is grayed out when:

- the editor isn't connected to a board;
- the flow on the board is the one on the canvas, deployed and unchanged since;
- the flow is stopped at the Python prompt (click **Restart Thingstudio**);
- the board is restarting.

## Module missing on the board

A deploy can fail with `ImportError: no module named '...'`: the flow needs a module the board's MicroPython doesn't
have. The board keeps running its previous flow.

The usual cause is networking. MQTT, UDP, HTTP and WiFi nodes need the `network` and `socket` modules, which only
boards with WiFi or Ethernet have. A Raspberry Pi Pico has neither; a Pico W does. If the board reports no WiFi, the
console warns you before the deploy.

Other modules differ between ports and builds. If the import is in your own function node, check the module exists
for your board in the [MicroPython docs](https://docs.micropython.org/). A board that should have it may need a
different [MicroPython build](https://micropython.org/download/).

Thingstudio's own libraries, such as the MQTT client and display drivers, are sent by Deploy. See
[Libraries](flow-lifecycle.md#libraries).

## MemoryError or a library that won't load

On an ESP32 without external RAM (PSRAM), a flow can fail to load with `MemoryError` even though the `[memory]` line
shows free RAM. The free RAM is in pieces, and the library needs one large piece. This is most likely after a display
flow has run. Use **Tools → Reset board (hard)**, then deploy again. See the [FAQ](faq.md) for why an ESP32 has
little room.

If Deploy says the board is **too full to receive the flow**, the running flow is using the memory. Use
**Tools → Remove flow…**, then **Tools → Reset board (hard)**, then deploy.

## WiFi Internal State Error on deploy

On an ESP32, deploying a flow with MQTT nodes can fail with "Wifi Internal State Error". The board is still
reconnecting to the network the previous flow used, and refuses a new connection until that finishes. The MQTT nodes
retry up to three times. If it still fails, deploy again.

## Reading a node error

When a node fails on the board, the console shows a `[NODE_ERROR]` line naming the node and the error, and the node
is highlighted on the canvas. Network nodes (`udp send`, `udp receive`, `http request`, `mqtt publish`,
`mqtt subscribe`) also name the operation and the host and port. A network node error without them is worth
[reporting](https://github.com/mkarliner/ThingStudio/issues).

## I2C device not answering

A sensor node's status dot shows **disconnected**, with "no reply at 0x76", when nothing answers at its address.
Scan the bus to see what is there. Type these two lines in the command box, one at a time, with your bus and pins:

```python
i2c = machine.I2C(0, scl=machine.Pin(5), sda=machine.Pin(4))
[hex(a) for a in i2c.scan()]
```

An [i2c device](nodes/i2c.md) node set to **scan** does the same from a flow.

An empty list means nothing answered. Check these, in order:

- The pin numbers. On a Pico, GP4 and GP5 are physical pins 6 and 7.
- SDA and SCL swapped.
- Power (3.3 V) and ground to the device.
- Solder joints on the header pins.

An address different from the node's means the address is wrong, not the wiring.

## A toggle button goes back

A [gui toggle](nodes/gui.md#a-toggle-that-follows-the-real-device) with its input wired shows the state you asked
for until the input confirms it. If nothing arrives within **wait for confirmation** (5 s by default), it goes back
to its last state, shows a cross for a moment, and the console shows
`NODE_ERROR ... NoConfirmation: no confirmation within 5 s`.

Check these, in order:

- The device is reachable and the command reached it. Watch the command topic with a debug node.
- The input is wired to the device's *state* topic, not the command topic.
- The state is sent in a form the toggle matches. A toggle set to `true` and `false` ignores `ON` and `OFF`: set its
  **value type** to text.

## Native code (Tools → Native code)

The `gs4`, `gs2` and `mono` frame formats of [display spi](nodes/display-spi.md) compile part of their code to
native machine code, which needs the right architecture for the board's chip.

**Tools → Native code** defaults to **Arch: Auto**, which uses the processor of the board in the
[Board menu](boards.md). If Deploy fails with an architecture or native-module error, pick your board's chip from
the list and deploy again.

## Restarting the board

A board can run short of memory after several deploys, or after a flow that uses a lot of it, such as a display.
The console suggests a restart when a deploy fails with `MemoryError`, the board restarts while starting a flow, or an
ESP32 has too little memory left for WiFi.

The Tools menu has two restarts:

- **Tools → Restart board (soft)** restarts MicroPython. The saved flow starts again with clean memory. USB stays
  connected.
- **Tools → Reset board (hard)** resets the whole chip, like its reset button, and frees all memory. A board with
  native USB (Pico, ESP32-S2, S3 and C3) disconnects; click **Connect** when it's back.

Try the soft restart first after a `MemoryError`. When an ESP32 is short of memory for WiFi, only the hard reset
gives it back. The console says which to use. Deploy is off until the board is back, which can take several seconds.

## Board stuck restarting

A flow that crashes the board as it starts would crash it on every restart. If the saved flow doesn't stay up for 10
seconds on three restarts in a row, the board starts without it, and the console shows **[safe mode]**. Fix the flow
and deploy it again, or remove it.

**Tools → Remove flow…** deletes the saved flow from the board, for any flow that stops the board answering:

1. Select the board's port and choose **Tools → Remove flow…**.
2. If the console asks, press the board's reset button. Thingstudio keeps trying for a minute.
3. When it's done, click **Connect**.

The board then starts with the runtime only, as after a fresh install. The flow on your canvas isn't affected.


---

Source: https://docs.thingstudio.net/faq/

# FAQ

## Why does my ESP32 have so little free memory?

An ESP32's RAM is shared between MicroPython and the chip's own software: ESP-IDF, its FreeRTOS scheduler, and
the WiFi stack. About half of a classic ESP32's 520 KB is taken before anything runs, by code that has to run from
RAM, the flash cache and fixed buffers. WiFi and the rest of ESP-IDF then take more as they run.

Measured on a CYD (classic ESP32, no external RAM) with a flow running:

| | KB |
|---|---|
| Used before the heap starts | ~287 |
| MicroPython's heap | 109 |
| ESP-IDF, FreeRTOS and WiFi, allocated while running | ~85 |
| Free | 33 |

So MicroPython gets about a fifth of the chip's RAM. The **[memory]** line in the console (shown at the **Info**
level) shows the current figures.

## Why does a Pico W have more room than an ESP32-C3, when the C3 has more RAM?

The Pico W's WiFi chip has its own processor and memory. On an ESP32 the whole WiFi stack runs on the main chip
and uses its RAM. So a 264 KB Pico W leaves more for your flow than a 400 KB ESP32-C3.

## Deploy failed with "MemoryError ... allocating 38400 bytes". Why, when there's more free memory than that?

Free memory is in pieces. A big buffer needs one piece that size, and after a while an ESP32 may not have
one. A 240x320 frame in 16 grays is 38,400 bytes. The [GUI nodes](nodes/gui.md) avoid this by drawing the
screen in strips. If your own `function` node builds a full frame, draw it in strips too, or restart
the board before deploying.

## Why does http request fail with "MemoryError" fetching a page?

The node reads the whole response body into memory at once. A page larger than the largest free block fails, even
when the console shows more free memory than the page size. A 56 KB page on an ESP32-C3 failed with
`MemoryError allocating 56722 bytes`; a 48-byte page worked. Point the node at a smaller response, or use a board
with PSRAM for large pages.

## My ESP32-S3 board has PSRAM, but the console shows only about 120 KB free. Why?

The firmware doesn't use the PSRAM. The generic ESP32-S3 build leaves it off. Flash the build for boards with
octal PSRAM (the `SPIRAM_OCT` variant) from [micropython.org/download](https://micropython.org/download/ESP32_GENERIC_S3/).
The console then shows megabytes free. Freenove's S3 display boards are an example: 121 KB before, 7.8 MB after.

## Which board should I use for a display and WiFi together?

An ESP32 with external RAM (PSRAM), such as many ESP32-S3 boards. MicroPython puts its heap in the external RAM,
leaving the chip's own RAM for WiFi. A classic ESP32 or ESP32-C3 without PSRAM can run a display and WiFi, but
only at lower color depths and with little to spare.

## My WiFi flow worked before, but now the board crashes or won't join. Why?

On an ESP32, MicroPython's heap grows by taking memory from ESP-IDF when a flow needs more, and keeps it until the
chip is reset. After a flow that uses a lot of memory, such as a display, WiFi may not have enough left to start.
The console warns you before you deploy. Use **Tools → Reset board (hard)**: a soft restart doesn't give that
memory back. See [Restarting the board](debugging.md#restarting-the-board).

## Why does Deploy say the board needs the runtime installed again?

The editor and the runtime on the board talk a shared protocol. When an update changes it, a board with the older
runtime can't run flows from the newer editor, so Deploy stops and says so. Use **Tools → Install runtime…**, then
Connect and deploy again.

## How do I tell which version of the editor I'm running?

It's next to **Thingstudio** in the toolbar, and in **Help → About**. A `+` after it means you built the editor
from uncommitted changes.

## My clock shows `--` and never the time. Why?

The ntp node hasn't synced yet. Its status says why: **waiting for WiFi**, or **NTP from *server* failed** when the
board can't reach the server. It tries again every 30 seconds. See [ntp](nodes/ntp.md#errors).

## My gui toggle shows `--`. Why?

A toggle with its input wired shows `--` until the input sends a value it recognises. It matches the input against
its *on sends* and *off sends* values, `true` and `false` unless you changed them. A Tasmota plug reports `ON` and
`OFF` as text: set the toggle's value type to text. See [a toggle that follows the real device](nodes/gui.md#a-toggle-that-follows-the-real-device).

## Why can't I use a touch node and a gui screen on the same panel?

Both would poll the same chip, and each would take touches from the other. A gui screen reads its panel itself.
Use the touch node only when you aren't using the GUI. Deploy stops and names both nodes if a panel is picked twice.

## Why won't a function node's output wire into pwm out?

A function node's output has the type `any`, and `pwm out`'s input takes a `number`. The editor refuses a wire from
`any` to `number`, `int` or `string` inputs. See [Wiring](working-in-the-editor.md#wiring).

## Why is Compile → Deploy grayed out after a deploy?

The board already runs the flow on the canvas. Deploy comes back when you change the flow. See
[Deploy is grayed out](debugging.md#deploy-is-grayed-out).

## Why are the pin fields dropdowns?

Your processor names its pins instead of numbering them. The STM32 on a pyboard uses `X1`, `A13` and so on. Pin
fields then list the chip's own pins rather than take a number. See
[Pins that aren't numbers](boards.md#pins-that-arent-numbers).

## Why can't I use SPI bus 0 or 1 on an nRF52840?

On the nRF52840, SPI 0 and 1 share hardware with I2C 0 and 1, so a flow using both would fail on the board.
Thingstudio offers SPI on buses 2 and 3 only. See [Boards and processors](boards.md#built-in-processors).

## Why did my saved settings reset after I renamed the flow?

Saved values are kept per flow name. Renaming the flow makes it a new name to the board, so its values start from
the defaults. The old values are still on the board: rename the flow back to use them again, or clear them from the
[command box](debugging.md#commands-and-the-python-prompt).

## Why doesn't my Uno TFT shield work on a Wemos D1 R32?

The D1 R32 puts the shield's A2, A3 and A4 on GPIO 35, 34 and 36, which are input only on an ESP32. A parallel
TFT shield drives its RS, CS and RST lines from those pins, so it can't start. Wire GPIO 15 to A2 (RS), GPIO 33
to A3 (CS) and GPIO 32 to A4 (RST), then set those pins in the display node.
